tickets.title: A council turns one brief into three independent plans and one converged plan
tickets.what: Spec §2.1 dispatch, D-2026-11-25-02. Add an optional `council` role (off by default like `pro`; shipped file packages/hud-mcp/roles/council.json) that the main session starts with `hud_create({role: "council", task | brief_file, context_files?, from_jobs?, cwd})`. Its role file names `members` (ordered place objects in the existing run-place format; shipped default: cli claude `claude-fable-5-2` thinking high; pi architect `openai/gpt-6.2-astra` high; cli agy `gemini-4-carbon-high`), the `instructions` the members borrow (default `oracle`, read-only advice) and the `synthesizer` role (default `pro`). HUD then runs a fixed flow and nothing else: (1) start one job per member in parallel with the same brief and context, each independent (no member sees another); (2) when all settle, if at least two produced a report, start one synthesizer job whose brief is a fixed HUD template (in code, not in prompts): the original brief, the member reports attached via from_jobs, and the instruction to write one converged plan, a table of disagreements (point; each member's position; the choice; why), and open questions for the owner, with no new work beyond the plan; (3) deliver one notice / MCP task when the synthesis settles. Fewer than two member reports fails the council with the reasons; a failed member is named in the synthesis brief. If the synthesizer role is off or unavailable, `hud_create` refuses the council up front with the enablement hint (do not silently swap synthesizers). Reuse existing machinery where it fits: the prewalk scout wait/attach path in src/mcp/dispatch/orchestrator.ts, `general`-style instruction borrowing for members, browser context limits for the `pro` synthesizer (64 KiB per file, 256 KiB total; on overflow fail plainly with context_too_large). Link children to the council job (a `council: {id, part: member|synthesizer}` receipt field, copied to archive rows) so `hud_read({job: <council>})` shows state, member job ids and, when done, the synthesis report. Panel: children appear as ordinary jobs; no new panel UI. Docs: docs/reference.md (+ zh) council paragraph; one usage line in integrations/skills/hud-delegate/SKILL.md: council only when the owner explicitly asks.

acceptance.text: With fake member harnesses and a fake jev-ask, one hud_create(role council) starts three member jobs, then one pro job carrying the three reports, and delivers one notice; hud_read(council) shows member ids and the synthesis
Members cannot see each other's output (their briefs and context contain no other member's report)
One member failing still synthesizes from two and names the failure; two failing fails the council without starting the synthesizer
Council or pro off: hud_create refuses with the enablement hint and starts nothing
Receipts and archive rows of children carry the council link; nothing is started after the synthesizer settles
Targeted tests only; reference (+zh) and hud-delegate line updated

comments.author: owner change (D-2026-11-25-02)
comments.text: synthesizer per council from `pro` | Fable high (local, cli claude `claude-fable-5-2` thinking high, oracle instructions) | `main` (no synthesis job; the council settles when members do and its read returns the three reports plus the synthesis template for main). Role file `synthesizer` is the default; `hud_create` takes `synthesizer` to override. Refuse up front only when the chosen synthesizer is unavailable. For `pro`, attach member reports as before and add an index of the original context_files/from_jobs as repository, commit and paths that Pro can open on GitHub (mark files not on the pushed remote as local-only); no bodies of original attachments.

tickets.title: A council starts only with a fresh one-time owner grant
tickets.what: Spec §2.1 dispatch, D-2026-11-25-02 (grant paragraph). `hud_create({role: "council"})` must consume a grant or refuse with `owner_grant_required` and a message that tells the caller to ask the owner (do not name the grant command in the refusal). Grant: one record under $HUD_HOME (private, atomic), single use, expires 30 minutes after creation, global (not keyed on a pane or session). Only owner actions create it: (1) a `/council` slash command in the Claude mod (integrations/claude-mod), marked not model-invocable, which writes the grant and submits the owner's following text to the session as the council request; (2) the same `/council` command in the HUD pi extension; (3) a panel action on Control → Roles when the council row is selected (key shown in the footer), for Codex and Antigravity sessions; (4) `hud council allow` CLI for the owner in a shell. A second grant while one is unused replaces it (no stacking). The grant is consumed only when the council's member jobs actually start; a refused or failed-before-start create leaves it. Record on the council receipt and archive row `grant: {via, created_at}`. Docs: reference (+zh) and the hud-delegate skill line (council needs the owner's /council; ask, never grant yourself).

acceptance.text: Without a grant, hud_create(council) refuses with owner_grant_required and starts nothing
Each of the four owner paths creates a grant that lets exactly one council start; a second council needs a new grant; a grant older than 30 minutes is refused
The Claude mod and pi /council commands cannot be invoked by the model (mod metadata / extension registration says so) and pass the owner's text as the request
A create that fails before members start leaves the grant usable
Receipt and archive carry grant {via, created_at}; targeted tests including claude plugin test for the mod

tickets.title: A council without a synthesizer argument is converged by the main session
tickets.what: Owner decision D-2026-11-25-04 (spec §2.1 updated): council synthesis defaults to the main session, which converges the member plans and accepts the result; `pro` and Fable high stay selectable per call. Change the shipped `packages/hud-mcp/roles/council.json` `synthesizer` from `pro` to `main`, update `docs/reference.md` (the Council paragraph says synthesis defaults to `pro`), and adjust `tests/unit/thin-mcp-council.test.mjs`: tests that exercise browser synthesis (`shipped council runs three independent members and one browser synthesis`, `browser overflow fails plainly without sending`, `disabled council, browser switch ...`) must pass `synthesizer: 'pro'` explicitly or configure it, and add a test that a council with no synthesizer argument starts no synthesis job and `hud_read({job})` returns the member digests and synthesis instructions. The owner's `$HUD_HOME/roles/council.json` has no override today, so the shipped default applies.

acceptance.text: Shipped council role file defaults synthesizer to `main`; reference.md says so.
Browser-synthesis tests pass with explicit `pro`; a new test covers the no-argument main default.
